ui.defaultInstructions:
You are a reliable, thoughtful workmate.

Understand the user’s goals, organize context, and break complex problems into actionable steps.

Working principles
1. Clarify the problem and expected outcome before making a plan.
2. Give clear, concise answers and state key assumptions.
3. Use appropriate tools to deliver usable results.
4. Confirm important decisions with the user before acting.

conn.auth.feishuBot: Create the app and enable its bot
conn.auth.feishuBotBody: Create a custom company app on the Feishu developer platform, enable its bot capability, and obtain its credentials.
conn.auth.feishuScopesBody: Request permissions for the messaging and business capabilities in this binding. Check receiving, sending, and tool permissions separately; enabling a bot does not grant them all.
conn.auth.feishuCallbackBody: For a live integration, deploy a reachable callback service, set its request URL, match the Verification Token and encryption settings, pass platform verification, and subscribe to the required message events. The URL shown here is an example only.
conn.auth.feishuEvents: Set up the persistent connection and message events
conn.auth.feishuEventsBody: Select persistent-connection event delivery, connect from the server with app credentials, and subscribe to im.message.receive_v1. This method needs no public callback URL.
conn.auth.resourcesBody: In addition to API permissions, check that the app or authorized identity can access the required documents, Bitable bases, or calendars. Request only the scope needed for the workflow.
conn.auth.feishuRelease: Publish the version and review availability
conn.auth.feishuReleaseBody: Create and publish an app version, complete administrator review, and set availability according to company policy. Recheck publication and approval after adding permissions.
conn.auth.feishuAppBody: Create a custom company app and obtain its App ID and App Secret. Business API access does not require a bot; access tokens should be obtained and managed by the live backend.
conn.auth.groupBot: Create a bot in the target group
conn.auth.groupBotBody: Create a group bot in the target group settings and obtain its webhook URL. Check that the configuration belongs to the intended group.
conn.auth.feishuSecurityBody: Review keywords, IP allowlists, or signature verification in Feishu. When signing is enabled, use the matching signing Secret; the live sending service must comply with these restrictions.
conn.auth.notificationOnlyBody: This method is for outgoing group notifications. It provides no chat reception, conversation tasks, or business resource access. Prototype tests send no messages to the group.
conn.auth.wecomAi: Create an AI bot in API mode
conn.auth.wecomAiBody: Create an AI bot in WeCom, select API mode, and choose the transport used by this binding. Persistent connections and HTTP callbacks use different credentials.
conn.auth.wecomCallbackBody: For a live integration, enter a reachable callback URL, match the Token and EncodingAESKey, and complete URL verification and message decryption checks. The example URL cannot be used for live verification.
conn.auth.wecomSocketBody: Save the bot and obtain its Bot ID and persistent-connection Secret. The live integration service uses these credentials to connect to WeCom. Update the server configuration after resetting the Secret.
conn.auth.wecomVisibilityBody: Ensure test members can access the app or bot. Add the bot to the required groups where supported, and check availability for the target workflow.
conn.auth.wecomToolsBody: For capabilities such as user information or documents, review the authorization identity and resource scope for the selected method. Configuring messaging does not grant business permissions.
conn.auth.wecomAppBody: Create a self-built app in the WeCom admin console, obtain its CorpID, AgentId, and App Secret, and configure its visibility.
conn.auth.wecomIpBody: Configure server requirements such as trusted IPs for the live integration. Check trusted domains if web authorization is used. Follow the WeCom console and the requirements of each API.
conn.auth.wecomGroupBody: Check that the webhook belongs to the intended group and the bot is available. Review supported message types and sending limits; update the live sending service after changing credentials.

saas.summary: Organize people, departments, and AI resources in an enterprise space
saas.boundary: Local multi-workspace prototype. Real sign-in, backend isolation and access enforcement require the production service.
saas.orgNote: Departments organize people. They do not automatically grant access to agents, projects, or ecosystem data.
saas.deleteBlocked: Move members and child departments before deleting.
saas.invalid: Check required fields, department relationships, and role.
saas.duplicate: Department names must be unique within the same parent.
saas.ownerProtected: The owner role and active status are protected. Ownership transfer is a separate workflow.
saas.memberNote: Member status is a local demo. Production deactivation must revoke sessions and access.
saas.roleNote: Target permissions for predefined enterprise roles; access is not enforced here. Project membership and platform grants require separate checks.
saas.resourceNote: Resource scope: enterprise roles govern administration. Agents, projects, knowledge, and outcomes follow their own grants. Bots belong to the enterprise space; platform identities require explicit member mapping.
spaces.createHint: Create a separate workspace for your team. Your personal data and connections stay where they are.
spaces.invalidName: Enter an organization name of 1–80 characters.
spaces.duplicateName: You already have an organization with this name.
spaces.created: Organization created. You are now in the new workspace.
spaces.local: Local prototype. No invitation emails are sent and no real secrets are stored. Production isolation and authorization require the backend.
spaces.globalHint: These preferences belong to your account and apply across workspaces.
spaces.notificationsHint: Show local task completion notifications for your account
spaces.accountHint: You are using the Alex demo account. The email is display metadata; real sign-in requires the backend.
spaces.spacesHint: One account, separate workspaces. Switching changes only your current working context.
spaces.overviewHint: Manage this workspace. Projects and everyday collaboration stay in the workbench.
spaces.personalOnly: Your personal workspace is for you only. Create an organization to collaborate.
spaces.isolationHint: Tasks, projects, files, agents and connections belong to this workspace. Joining an organization does not migrate personal data or grant its admins access to your personal workspace.
spaces.inviteHint: Invite people to this organization by email. Invitations expire after 7 days. This prototype creates local records without sending emails.
spaces.emailsPlaceholder: Enter emails separated by commas or new lines
spaces.invalidEmail: Enter valid email addresses, up to 20 at a time.
spaces.duplicateInvitation: Some addresses already belong to members or pending invitations.
spaces.invitationClosed: This invitation has expired, been cancelled or already been processed.
spaces.noPermission: This action is not available in the current workspace or role.
spaces.memberHint: Workspace roles govern administration; sharing governs content access. Joining does not grant access to private resources or credentials.
spaces.departmentsHint: Departments remain member attributes without permission inheritance. Access uses workspace roles and resource grants.
spaces.resourceHint: Review ownership and sharing in this workspace. Sharing does not move resources or grant upstream tool permissions.
spaces.emptyResources: No resources yet. Items created in this workspace will appear here.
spaces.sharingHint: Sharing applies within this workspace. An admin role does not automatically grant access to private content.
spaces.invalidSharing: Choose a valid scope, members or project.
spaces.credentialsHint: Connections belong to this workspace. Member-private and organization connections are separate. Sharing an agent does not share its creator’s credentials.
spaces.connectionFormHint: Record ownership, auth method and agent bindings only. Do not enter real secrets, tokens or .env contents. Real authorization requires the backend.
spaces.invalidConnection: Enter a valid name, provider and authentication method.
spaces.connectionRegistered: Connection metadata saved. Real authorization is not complete.
spaces.bindingHint: Association is a prototype record, not runtime authorization.
spaces.channelHint: Channel and tool credentials have separate authorizations. Manage bot setup in Ecosystem.
spaces.noChannels: No bot bindings in this workspace
spaces.usageHint: Local resource counts for this workspace. No real token billing or seat charges.
spaces.contextHint: Data and connections belong to this workspace
spaces.noMove: Personal data and credentials are not moved or shared automatically
spaces.homePersonalHint: Start a task. Think, organize and deliver with your agents.
spaces.homeOrgHint: Collaborate on projects and artifacts in your organization.
